THOUGHT: This older man had a sudden, brief loss of consciousness without prodrome while ambulating. Key findings are a baseline ECG with right bundle branch block + left anterior fascicular block (bifascicular block) and an electrophysiology study showing a markedly prolonged baseline HV interval (88 ms) with dramatic prolongation to 211 ms on atrial pacing and induction of infra‑Hisian block. Those EP findings localize conduction disease to the His–Purkinje system and are diagnostic of intermittent high‑grade/complete AV block at the infra‑His level, which readily explains transient syncope from transient asystole or severely slowed ventricular escape. Normal troponins and echocardiogram make acute ischemia or structural pump failure unlikely. Other reasonable alternatives (sick sinus syndrome, ventricular tachyarrhythmia, neurally mediated syncope, orthostatic/medication‑induced hypotension or carotid sinus hypersensitivity) are less likely given the objective EP evidence of infra‑His conduction block but remain possible considerations in the differential.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Paroxysmal high‑grade (infra‑Hisian) atrioventricular block / intermittent complete heart block due to His–Purkinje conduction disease (most likely given bifascicular block and abnormal HV interval with inducible infra‑His block)
2. Advanced multifascicular conduction disease causing intermittent AV block (closely related to #1; alternative phrasing emphasizing multilevel conduction system disease)
3. Sick sinus syndrome (sinus node dysfunction causing transient bradycardia/asystole) — less likely given EP localization to infra‑His but still a possible bradyarrhythmic cause of syncope
4. Ventricular tachyarrhythmia (sustained VT causing syncope) — less likely given normal EF, no ischemic markers, and diagnostic EP findings pointing to AV block
5. Neurally mediated (vasovagal) syncope or reflex syncope / carotid sinus hypersensitivity or orthostatic/medication‑induced hypotension — possible common causes of syncope but unlikely here given absence of prodrome, negative orthostatic testing, and objective conduction system abnormality.
ground_truth: Bifascicular block with infra-Hisian Wenckebach block
